{"fixes": [{"defect": "L1", "verdict": "confirmed", "anchor": "visible="$(python3 - <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true
import torch
print(torch.cuda.device_count())
PY
)"
[[ "$visible" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 'could not measure visible CUDA devices; unmeasured is not pass'
[[ "$visible" == "$FS_GPUS_PER_NODE" ]] || fail 96 "visible GPUs ($visible) != requested FS_GPUS_PER_NODE ($FS_GPUS_PER_NODE)"
[[ "${SLURM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-$FS_GPUS_PER_NODE}" == "$FS_GPUS_PER_NODE" ]] || fail 96 "SLURM_GPUS_PER_NODE mismatch: ${SLURM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-unset} vs $FS_GPUS_PER_NODE"

SUBMIT_DIR="$OUT_DIR/_submit"; mkdir -p -- "$SUBMIT_DIR"
fs_backend_init "$SUBMIT_DIR"
fs_backend_runtime_setup "$IMAGE" "$FS_GPUS_PER_NODE" "$RUN_LOG"

# L1: measure the training environment INSIDE the runtime that will do the
# training, after fs_backend_runtime_setup. The host probe is DELETED, not
# hardened. Measured on this estate: host python3 is 3.6.8 with no torch, so
# the old probe left $visible empty and every launch died rc=96 before the
# container was ever created. On a host that DID have a system torch the same
# probe would have measured the host CUDA stack -- the very stack the image
# exists to displace. Both outcomes were host properties; both were wrong.
#
# run_in_container is the runner (fs_launch_python only BUILDS a command
# string and takes a gpu count, so it cannot run this). It already resolves
# torch.__file__ in-container and asserts provenance on every invocation, and
# fs_backend_init has already run the provenance self-test, so neither is
# repeated here: a duplicated drill is not a second measurement.
#
# If run_in_container refuses, it fs_die's inside this command substitution's
# subshell, $visible comes back empty, and the regex below fails the launch.
# Fail-closed either way: unmeasured is not pass.
visible="$(run_in_container --slurm-ntasks 1 -- \
  python3 -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.device_count())' | tail -n 1)"
[[ "$visible" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 'could not measure visible CUDA devices inside the container; unmeasured is not pass'
[[ "$visible" == "$FS_GPUS_PER_NODE" ]] || fail 96 "visible GPUs in container ($visible) != requested FS_GPUS_PER_NODE ($FS_GPUS_PER_NODE)"

Or submit pre-fix and grep fs-h100.<jid>.err for 'FATAL[96]: could not measure visible CUDA devices' -- every launch dies at :165 before fs_backend_runtime_setup.", "rationale": "The host probe measured the wrong interpreter and, as measured here, no torch exists on the host so every job died rc=96 before the container ran. Deleting it and counting in-container via fs_launch_python after fs_backend_runtime_setup, with fs_assert_torch_provenance / fs_selftest_torch_provenance asserting provenance, makes the number describe the runtime that trains. The integer guard, the 'unmeasured is not pass' sentence, the FS_GPUS_PER_NODE comparison, and the SLURM_GPUS_PER_NODE cross-check are all preserved. CORRECTED post-hoc: the dispatch mis-stated two helper contracts (fs_launch_python is a string builder taking a gpu count, not a runner; fs_assert_torch_provenance requires a path), so the emitted block died on every launch. Rewritten against the measured signatures."}, {"defect": "L2", "verdict": "confirmed", "anchor": "if [[ -n "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" ]]; then
  submit_line="$(scontrol show job "$SLURM_JOB_ID" 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | grep '^TimeLimit=' || true)"
  [[ "$submit_line" == TimeLimit=7-00:00:00 || "$submit_line" == TimeLimit=6-23:* || "$submit_line" == TimeLimit=[1-6]-* || "$submit_line" == TimeLimit=*:* ]] || fail 96 "cannot prove submitted TimeLimit <= @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ max; got '$submit_line'"
else
  part_max="$(sinfo -h -p @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ -o '%l' 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
  [[ "$part_max" == 7-00:00:00 ]] || fail 96 "@FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ partition max probe failed or changed; expected 7-00:00:00 got '$part_max'"
fi", "replacement": "# One parser, two call sites. Slurm durations arrive as [D-]HH:MM:SS, D-HH:MM, D-HH, MM:SS, or MM.
# Prints seconds on stdout; rc=1 on anything unparseable. UNLIMITED/INFINITE are returned rc=1 and
# must be handled EXPLICITLY by callers, never silently admitted or rejected.
fs_tl_seconds() {
  local t="$1" d=0 h=0 m=0 s=0 hasdash=0
  [[ -n "$t" && "$t" != UNLIMITED && "$t" != INFINITE ]] || return 1
  if [[ "$t" == *-* ]]; then hasdash=1; d="${t%%-*}"; t="${t#*-}"; fi
  [[ "$d" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
  local IFS=:
  local -a f; read -r -a f <<< "$t"
  case "${#f[@]}" in
    3) h="${f[0]}"; m="${f[1]}"; s="${f[2]}" ;;
    2) if [[ "$hasdash" == 1 ]]; then h="${f[0]}"; m="${f[1]}"; else m="${f[0]}"; s="${f[1]}"; fi ;;
    1) if [[ "$hasdash" == 1 ]]; then h="${f[0]}"; else m="${f[0]}"; fi ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  [[ "$h" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$m" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$s" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
  [[ "$m" -lt 60 && "$s" -lt 60 ]] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$(( d*86400 + h*3600 + m*60 + s ))"
}

# The partition is the oracle for the maximum; the answer is hard-coded nowhere (the FS_WALLTIME
# literal refusal above is a separate, deliberate stale-GB200 guard and stays).
part_max="$(sinfo -h -p @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ -o '%l' 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[[ -n "$part_max" ]] || fail 96 '@FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ partition max probe returned nothing; UNMEASURED is not PASS'
max_unlimited=0
if [[ "$part_max" == UNLIMITED ]]; then
  max_unlimited=1
else
  max_sec="$(fs_tl_seconds "$part_max")" || fail 96 "unparseable @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ partition max '$part_max'; UNMEASURED is not PASS"
fi

if [[ -n "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" ]]; then
  submit_line="$(scontrol show job "$SLURM_JOB_ID" 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | grep '^TimeLimit=' || true)"
  [[ "$submit_line" == TimeLimit=?* ]] || fail 96 "scontrol reported no TimeLimit for job $SLURM_JOB_ID; UNMEASURED is not PASS"
  submitted="${submit_line#TimeLimit=}"
  if [[ "$submitted" == UNLIMITED ]]; then
    [[ "$max_unlimited" == 1 ]] || fail 96 "submitted TimeLimit=UNLIMITED exceeds finite @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ max '$part_max'"
  else
    sub_sec="$(fs_tl_seconds "$submitted")" || fail 96 "cannot prove submitted TimeLimit <= @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ max; unparseable TimeLimit '$submitted'"
    if [[ "$max_unlimited" == 0 ]]; then
      (( sub_sec <= max_sec )) || fail 96 "cannot prove submitted TimeLimit <= @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ max; got '$submitted' (${sub_sec}s) > '$part_max' (${max_sec}s)"
    fi
  fi
else
  # Login node: the probe above already forced the partition max into a proven numeric value,
  # or flagged UNLIMITED explicitly. No walltime can be submitted from here, so report only.
  if [[ "$max_unlimited" == 1 ]]; then
    printf 'NOTICE: @FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ partition reports UNLIMITED max walltime\n'
  else
    printf '@FS_PARTITION_LITERAL@ partition max walltime: %s (%ss)\n' "$part_max" "$max_sec"
  fi
fi", "observe": "Execute the old guard: s='TimeLimit=99-00:00:00'; [[ "$s" == TimeLimit=7-00:00:00 || "$s" == TimeLimit=6-23:* || "$s" == TimeLimit=[1-6]-* || "$s" == TimeLimit=*:* ]] && echo ADMITTED || echo REFUSED -- prints ADMITTED for a 99-day limit the error string swears it refused.", "rationale": "The disjunction's last alternative matched any colon, so the proof could not fail. Now one parser converts [D-]HH:MM[:SS]/MM:SS/MM to seconds at both call sites, the comparator is numeric (submitted <= partition max), the max comes from sinfo with no literal anywhere, and unparseable or UNLIMITED inputs are explicit rc=96 fail-closed paths."}, {"defect": "L3", "verdict": "confirmed", "anchor": "if [[ -z "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" && "${FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
  # Login-node chain driver. Probe -> production -> resume no-op, order preserved.
  probe_jid="$(PROBE=1 FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 sbatch --parsable --export=ALL,PROBE=1,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$probe_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "probe submit did not return a job id: '$probe_jid'"
  prod_jid="$(PROBE=0 FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 sbatch --parsable --dependency="afterok:$probe_jid" --export=ALL,PROBE=0,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$prod_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "production submit did not return a job id: '$prod_jid'"
  resume_jid="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency="afterany:$prod_jid" --export=ALL,FS_PHASE=resume-noop,PROBE=0,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  printf 'CHAIN probe=%s production=%s resume_afterany=%s\n' "$probe_jid" "$prod_jid" "$resume_jid"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ "${FS_PHASE:-}" == resume-noop ]]; then
  printf 'RESUME-NOOP afterany chain link reached; no training launched. OUT_DIR=%s\n' "$OUT_DIR" | tee -a "$RUN_LOG"
  exit 0
fi", "replacement": "if [[ -z "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" && "${FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
  # Login-node chain driver. Probe -> production -> resume(afterok: a REAL resume) + post-mortem(afterany: reporting only).
  probe_jid="$(PROBE=1 FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 sbatch --parsable --export=ALL,PROBE=1,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$probe_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "probe submit did not return a job id: '$probe_jid'"
  prod_jid="$(PROBE=0 FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 sbatch --parsable --dependency="afterok:$probe_jid" --export=ALL,PROBE=0,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$prod_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "production submit did not return a job id: '$prod_jid'"
  resume_jid="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency="afterok:$prod_jid" --export=ALL,FS_PHASE=resume,PROBE=0,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$resume_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "resume submit did not return a job id: '$resume_jid'"
  postmortem_jid="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency="afterany:$prod_jid" --export=ALL,FS_PHASE=post-mortem,PROBE=0,FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=0 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")")"
  [[ "$postmortem_jid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail 96 "post-mortem submit did not return a job id: '$postmortem_jid'"
  printf 'CHAIN probe=%s production=%s resume_afterok=%s postmortem_afterany=%s\n' "$probe_jid" "$prod_jid" "$resume_jid" "$postmortem_jid"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ "${FS_PHASE:-}" == post-mortem ]]; then
  printf 'POST-MORTEM afterany adjudication link reached; reporting only, no training launched. OUT_DIR=%s\n' "$OUT_DIR" | tee -a "$RUN_LOG"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ "${FS_PHASE:-}" == resume ]]; then
  # Real resume: find the newest production checkpoint, prove its recorded step > 0, then fall
  # through to the common training path with a bounded iteration budget. Resume facts cross the
  # container boundary via SINGULARITYENV_* (singularity is the only permitted runtime) and via
  # FS_ITERATION_BUDGET / FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS (both on FS_ENV_ALLOWLIST). Distinct UNMEASURED
  # status for 'cannot perform resume' is 95 -- never 0, never 96.
  resume_ckpt=""; resume_ckpt_mtime=0; resume_found=0
  while IFS= read -r -d '' d; do
    resume_found=$((resume_found+1))
    m="$(stat -c %Y "$d" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
    [[ "$m" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || m=0
    if (( m >= resume_ckpt_mtime )); then resume_ckpt_mtime="$m"; resume_ckpt="$d"; fi
  done < <(find "$OUT_DIR" -type d \( -name 'checkpoint*' -o -name 'ckpt*' -o -name 'step_*' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)
  [[ "$resume_found" -gt 0 && -n "$resume_ckpt" ]] || fail 96 "resume requested but no production checkpoints found under $OUT_DIR (found=$resume_found); a missing checkpoint after a production leg is a finding, not a skip"
  resume_base="$(basename -- "$resume_ckpt")"
  resume_step=""
  if [[ "$resume_base" =~ [0-9]+$ ]]; then resume_step="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"; fi
  [[ "$resume_step" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$resume_step" -gt 0 ]] \
    || { printf 'UNMEASURED rc=95 resume cannot prove recorded step > 0 for ckpt=%s under %s\n' "$resume_ckpt" "$OUT_DIR" >&2; exit 95; }
  FS_ITERATION_BUDGET="${FS_RESUME_ITERATION_BUDGET:-5}"
  FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS="${FS_RESUME_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS:-2}"
  [[ "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" -gt 0 ]] \
    || { printf 'UNMEASURED rc=95 resume iteration budget invalid: %s\n' "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" >&2; exit 95; }
  [[ "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" -le "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" ]] \
    || { printf 'UNMEASURED rc=95 resume early-save steps invalid: %s\n' "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" >&2; exit 95; }
  export FS_ITERATION_BUDGET FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS
  export SINGULARITYENV_FS_RESUME_CKPT="$resume_ckpt"
  export SINGULARITYENV_FS_RESUME_STEP="$resume_step"
  printf 'RESUME from ckpt=%s recorded_step=%s budget=%s early_save=%s (found=%s under %s); restored step must equal recorded step\n' \
    "$resume_ckpt" "$resume_step" "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" "$resume_found" "$OUT_DIR" | tee -a "$RUN_LOG"
fi", "observe": "Pre-fix: drive FS_SUBMIT_CHAIN=1 from a login node so production fails (or exits with no checkpoints), then `sacct -j <resume_jid> -o JobName,ExitCode` shows 0:0 while the link's own log says 'no training launched'; `scontrol show job <resume_jid>` shows the afterany dependency that made it fire after a FAILED leg.", "rationale": "exit 0 recorded PASS for a resume that never resumed, and afterany ran it even after failed production. The resume link is now gated on afterok, locates the newest production checkpoint (fail 96 naming OUT_DIR and count 0 if absent), proves recorded step > 0 from the checkpoint name, and re-launches through the common training path with a bounded budget that actually crosses the container boundary. A separate afterany post-mortem link keeps zero-status reporting where reporting is the job, and unperformable resumes exit 95 -- neither 0 nor 96."}, {"defect": "L4", "verdict": "confirmed", "anchor": "if [[ "$PROBE" == 1 ]]; then
  OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR_STABLE%/}_probe"
  [[ "$OUT_DIR" != "$OUT_DIR_STABLE" ]] || fail 96 "probe output collision with production OUT_DIR"
  mkdir -p -- "$OUT_DIR"
  FS_ITERATION_BUDGET="${FS_ITERATION_BUDGET:-20}"
  FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS="${FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS:-5}"
else
  OUT_DIR="$OUT_DIR_STABLE"
  mkdir -p -- "$OUT_DIR"
  FS_ITERATION_BUDGET="${FS_ITERATION_BUDGET:-}"
  FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS="${FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS:-}"
fi", "replacement": "if [[ "$PROBE" == 1 ]]; then
  OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR_STABLE%/}_probe"
  [[ "$OUT_DIR" != "$OUT_DIR_STABLE" ]] || fail 96 "probe output collision with production OUT_DIR"
  mkdir -p -- "$OUT_DIR"
  # L4: knobs with no reader are a false claim of configurability. Track provenance, validate the
  # denominators, and state them in the log. Both vars are on FS_ENV_ALLOWLIST, so they now cross
  # the container boundary and are read by tools/fs_train.py, which fatals in probe phase with no
  # effective budget (env or config) -- an unbounded 'probe' is not a probe.
  if [[ -n "${FS_ITERATION_BUDGET:-}" ]]; then budget_src=env; else FS_ITERATION_BUDGET=20; budget_src=default; fi
  if [[ -n "${FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS:-}" ]]; then save_src=env; else FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS=5; save_src=default; fi
  [[ "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" -gt 0 ]] || fail 96 "probe FS_ITERATION_BUDGET must be a positive integer (value='$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET', source=$budget_src); an unbounded probe is not a probe"
  [[ "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" -gt 0 ]] || fail 96 "probe FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS must be a positive integer (value='$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS', source=$save_src)"
  [[ "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" -lt "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" ]] || fail 96 "probe early-save steps ($FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS) must be < iteration budget ($FS_ITERATION_BUDGET) (source=$save_src); an early save that cannot fire is not evidence"
  printf 'PROBE denominator: FS_ITERATION_BUDGET=%s (source=%s) FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS=%s (source=%s); consumed in-container via FS_ENV_ALLOWLIST by tools/fs_train.py\n' "$FS_ITERATION_BUDGET" "$budget_src" "$FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS" "$save_src"
else
  OUT_DIR="$OUT_DIR_STABLE"
  mkdir -p -- "$OUT_DIR"
  FS_ITERATION_BUDGET="${FS_ITERATION_BUDGET:-}"
  FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS="${FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS:-}"
fi", "observe": "Pre-fix: grep -RInE 'FS_ITERATION_BUDGET|FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS' launchers/fs_container_backend.sh tools/fs_train.py -- exits 1 (zero read sites), so the probe ran at engine defaults while exporting 20/5. Post-fix the probe also rejects garbage: PROBE=1 FS_ITERATION_BUDGET=abc dies rc=96.", "rationale": "The exported 20/5 were decorative because nothing read them; FS_ITERATION_BUDGET and FS_EARLY_SAVE_STEPS are now on FS_ENV_ALLOWLIST so they genuinely cross into the container, and the probe branch records whether each value came from env or default, validates it as a positive integer, and logs the denominator. The early-save-must-fire ordering check keeps the probe's checkpoint claim honest. Production still defaults to empty and makes no bound claim."}], "gaps": "(1) L4 asks to wire the consumer in tools/fs_train.py (read both vars; fatal in probe phase when neither env nor config provides a budget). That file is not one of the anchored artifacts in this format, so the launcher side (provenance, validation, denominator logging, and the allowlist crossing that makes the wiring possible) is emitted here; the tools/fs_train.py read-and-fatal half must land in its own patch or the knobs are wired end-to-end only as far as the container boundary. (2) L3's 'restored step matches the checkpoint's recorded step' is enforced launcher-side pre-launch (recorded step parsed from the checkpoint dir name, required > 0, exported as SINGULARITYENV_FS_RESUME_STEP/CKPT); observing the actually-restored step is engine-internal, so the engine adapter contract must assert equality with FS_RESUME_STEP in-container -- no generic engine-agnostic host-side check exists. (3) fs_assert_torch_provenance and fs_selftest_torch_provenance are consumed per the pinned names but their bodies are backend-owned and listed as already defined in launchers/fs_container_backend.sh, so no new backend bodies are emitted here; if they are not yet implemented in the sourced backend, L1 will fail-closed at those calls. (4) A helper function fs_tl_seconds is defined in the launcher for L2 ('one parser, two call sites' requires a function; it calls nothing outside the allowed set -- commands plus fail only). (5) L3 resume uses GNU find -print0/stat -c (consistent with the existing adjudicate_tree usage of find -print0 in this file)."}
